source.name: sp_GetTopCustomers
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_GetTopCustomers
    @TopN INT = 10
AS
BEGIN
    SELECT TOP (@TopN)
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        ISNULL(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        DATEDIFF(DAY, MAX(o.OrderDate), GETDATE()) AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_GetTopCustomers(
    p_TopN INT DEFAULT 10
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    CustomerID INT,
    FullName VARCHAR,
    OrderCount BIGINT,
    TotalSpent NUMERIC,
    DaysSinceLastOrder INT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        COALESCE(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - MAX(o.OrderDate)))::INT AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC
    LIMIT p_TopN;
END;
$$;
assumptions: The 'dbo' schema exists in PostgreSQL database
CustomerID column is of type INT in both Customers and Orders tables
FirstName and LastName are VARCHAR or TEXT types
TotalAmount is a numeric type (NUMERIC, DECIMAL, or similar)
OrderDate is a DATE or TIMESTAMP type
The procedure returns a result set, so converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
Parameter renamed from @TopN to p_TopN following PostgreSQL naming conventions

reviewFlags.reason: Verify the actual data type of CustomerID in the Customers and Orders tables. It may be BIGINT, SERIAL, or another integer type.
VARCHAR without length specified. Consider using TEXT or VARCHAR with explicit length based on FirstName and LastName column definitions.
Verify the actual data type and precision of TotalAmount column in Orders table. May need NUMERIC(precision, scale) or DECIMAL.

DATEDIFF conversion assumes OrderDate is DATE or TIMESTAMP. If OrderDate is DATE type, consider using (CURRENT_DATE - MAX(o.OrderDate))::INT for cleaner syntax. Result may differ if time components are involved.
Ensure the calling application expects a function instead of a procedure and can handle the TABLE return type.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server procedure returns result set implicitly. PostgreSQL function must be called with SELECT * FROM dbo.sp_GetTopCustomers(10) instead of EXEC dbo.sp_GetTopCustomers 10.

SQL Server uses + operator for string concatenation, PostgreSQL uses || operator. NULL handling differs: SQL Server returns NULL if any operand is NULL, PostgreSQL CONCAT function handles NULLs but || does not.

DATEDIFF(DAY, ...) in SQL Server vs EXTRACT(DAY FROM interval) in PostgreSQL may produce different results when time components are involved. SQL Server DATEDIFF counts date boundaries crossed, PostgreSQL EXTRACT returns the day component of the interval.
ISNULL converted to COALESCE. Both functions behave similarly for two arguments, but COALESCE is SQL standard.
SQL Server TOP clause converted to PostgreSQL LIMIT. Both produce equivalent results when used with ORDER BY.
